## Natural history notes

A small aquatic true bug characterized by an oval, flattened body, short beak, and oar-like hind legs used for swimming through the water. In Florida, Corisella edulis is the Florida-recorded member of its genus and occurs in freshwater habitats such as ponds, lakes, marshes, ditches, canals, and slow vegetated waters. Like other water boatmen, it swims right-side-up and feeds mostly by scraping or gathering algae, detritus, and fine organic material from submerged surfaces, while also serving as prey for fish, amphibians, and larger aquatic insects.
